```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a paying customer within 90 days. A has documented willingness to pay from the exact buyer. SwagUp publishes paid tiers of $99 to $999 per month plus fulfillment fees. Hampton, BurnRate and Endcrawl are named companies that pay for welcome swag or swag automation. B has zero paying comparables: every competitor is free or donation-supported.",
    "B's strongest market signal is negative. Fakespot was well-funded and well-distributed, yet it shut down in July 2025, which suggests the category struggles to monetize even at scale.",
    "A's payer is a business with budget, reachable one founder at a time. One B2B customer is enough to hit the goal, and heavy competition does not stop a single sale. B needs consumers to switch from several already-installed free alternatives to a paid tier.",
    "A's demand evidence comes from buyers describing spend and pain in their own words. B's demand evidence is mostly launch posts by builders of free tools. It includes a counter-signal calling such detectors 'downright immoral' and no statement of intent to pay.",
    "B carries extra risks that A does not. AI-detection accuracy is unsolved and false positives draw backlash. Reddit can unilaterally restrict third-party tooling. Free-tier LLM costs also fall on the builder.",
    "A has serious weaknesses. Incumbents already offer the Stripe-trigger mechanic, margins are thin, and physical fulfillment is operationally heavy. Several cost and customs claims are cited by name only, with no link: Merchloop/PerkUp kit costs and the customs breakdown. These hurt long-term defensibility more than the odds of landing a first paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's price anchor. The $3-5/month Pro tier rests on GPTZero's $10-15 tier, which serves a different use case and buyer. It also rests on a 'typical' $4.99/month consumer extension subscription, which has no source. No evidence shows any user of a Reddit or review filter paying or offering to pay, so willingness to pay is effectively missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A clearly beats B on evidence that someone will pay, which is the deciding factor for a 90-day paying customer. A's own brief admits it lacks a defensible wedge against incumbents that already ship the feature, so A is the better first bet but not a strong one. Some of A's supporting claims are cited by name only, with no link, which slightly weakens its case."
}
```
